steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Here we are, Miss Baker. My condolences.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: May I see her?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: She looks peaceful... like she wasn't in too much pain.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: She was in the final stages of her disease, and she insisted further treatment was pointless. Most of the plans the doctors came up with were palliative, and so...

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: So they gave her a lot of suppressants.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: (Wipes tears from eyes)

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: A while ago, she wrote me a letter to tell me she was sick. I was gonna head back as soon as I could to pay her a visit, but I couldn't take time off work.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: When I finally got a few days off and made it to the hospital, her bed was already empty. I asked the nurse, and she gave me this address.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: It's a good thing you came today... If you were just a day later, I'm afraid you wouldn't have been able to see her. According to the schedule, she's going to be cremated tonight.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Right. So I came just in time.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Sorry, I didn't mean it like that...

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: No, I'm not trying to blame you. I'm just lamenting.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Are you okay? I can bring you a chair, if you need it.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: No thanks... Did she leave any personal effects?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Um... We found lots of cosmetics in the apartment she rented. There was also glue, clay, oil paintings, wigs, and some really scary-looking props.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I guess the room probably looked like a serial killer's hideout.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Right, we cleared out six cans of fake blood from that room... not to mention the fake limbs and eyeballs.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Was there anything else?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Oh, she was holding a notebook when she died.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Can I see it?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Give me a minute. I'll get it for you.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Here. To tell the truth, as someone who works in a morgue, I can say for certain that this is the scariest thing I've ever seen in my entire life.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: (Flips through the pages) ...

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I didn't expect her to hold onto my pictures.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: This scary old woman here... Is that you?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Yeah, we used to practice on each other. The monster with the pustules all over is her.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Hm? Is that a letter?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: 'For Baker.'

a.text: You awful bitch. It's been ages since I sent you that video tape. The least you could've done is write back, whether you've watched it or not. Mario and I knew The Living Dead on the Frontier was going to bomb in the theaters.

spans.text: You awful bitch. It's been ages since I sent you that video tape. The least you could've done is write back, whether you've watched it or not. Mario and I knew
The Living Dead on the Frontier
was going to bomb in the theaters.

a.text: We had a tight deadline and a tight budget. By the time we were in post, both of us were stretched thin. The only thing that wasn't tight was our pants, with our waistlines shrinking by the day, starved as we were. Mario's still going to get his next picture financed, but most of the producers know his reputation. No one is giving him any money.

spans.text: We had a tight deadline and a tight budget. By the time we were in post, both of us were stretched thin. The only thing that wasn't tight was our pants, with our waistlines shrinking by the day, starved as we were. Mario's still going to get his next picture financed, but most of the producers know his reputation. No one is giving him any money.

a.text: I was thinking of helping out after I got discharged, but the doctors all had such long faces. They insisted on me staying in the hospital. The days here are boring, and that got me reminiscing about the old days. That room in the basement we spent all that time in, the ice cold beers with white foam, and the movies we never got tired of...

spans.text: I was thinking of helping out after I got discharged, but the doctors all had such long faces. They insisted on me staying in the hospital. The days here are boring, and that got me reminiscing about the old days. That room in the basement we spent all that time in, the ice cold beers with white foam, and the movies we never got tired of...

a.text: I'm really scared. I'm scared I'll die alone. If you get the time, could you come visit me?

spans.text: I'm really scared. I'm scared I'll die alone. If you get the time, could you come visit me?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: I'm really sorry. We were too careless and didn't notice the letter. If we'd found it, we would've contacted you immediately.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: It's okay. The stuff drawn on here is scary. I get how hard it'd be to look over everything.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Still, it's an oversight on our part.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Even if you managed to get in touch with me, it wouldn't have changed anything. I just would've found out she died sooner.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: *sigh*... Once they're dead, they're gone forever. Miss Baker, at the end of the day, you're here. She'll have someone to send her off as she departs on her final journey.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Is there anything I can do?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Nothing. I cleaned her body yesterday, got her out of her hospital gown, and changed her into some proper clothes.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Thanks for that.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: I was just doing my job. In a minute, I'll put on some makeup. She'll look much better.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Makeup? Is that something you usually do?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Oh, it's just some broad strokes. There's really nothing that special to it.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Is it okay... if I do it?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Well... Are you sure about that? Knowing who you are...

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I don't mind, and I just so happen to have all the tools I need on me.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Let me do her makeup one last time, like the old days.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Yeah... I guess I couldn't do it as good as you.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Now that's not true. You're the expert here when it comes to embalming. I'm sure I'll have questions for you later.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Not at all...

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: (Wipes the deceased's face)

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Do you know... how she died?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Chronic poisoning. The doctors think it's because of long-term exposure to cheap, low quality paint. The staff who handled her belongings also complained about how pungent those things all were.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: You don't seem surprised.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: When a low budget production finally gets funded, who'd spend the money on a makeup artist instead of a couple more hot actresses? Of course they'd just keep pinching pennies on every opportunity they got.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: And I warned her about this a long time ago...

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: (Looks up and blinks)

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Never mind. It's all in the past now.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: (Picks up the brush)

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Why did you stop?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I've never done makeup on the dead. She's here, but she can't say a single word to me. I really don't know how she wanted herself to look in the end.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Actually, when we apply makeup to the dead, we don't always do it the way they'd want. Sometimes, we do it the way their family wants them to look.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Just make her look the way you'd want.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: The way I'd want...?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: That's right. The most beautiful she ever looked in your memories.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: The most beautiful she's looked...

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: Hey, Baker! Baker! Something on your mind?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Cynthia! I've waited for you for a whole hour! You know that?!

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: Sorry, this meal's on me, okay?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Where have you been?

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: I ran into Mario around the corner, so I talked to him for the better part of the day. I got no idea who he ripped off this time, but he came up with the money to start shooting his next picture.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: He never knows when to give up, huh?

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: You know, I'm not one to give up, either!

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I know, but the last couple times you two worked together... really bombed. You know what the stuck-up critics call him? 'Box Office Poison,' 'Wrankwood's Tumor.'

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: Hmph, the same people called him 'Father of the Slasher' and 'Master of Horror' fifteen years ago.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Cynthia, it's time for us both to admit that slasher flicks are out. Mario's time has come and gone.

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: Do you remember that time we got together in the basement and watched The Vault of Gore together. It's what inspired us to become makeup artists.

spans.text: Do you remember that time we got together in the basement and watched
together. It's what inspired us to become makeup artists.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: The bizarre, horrifyingly lifelike looks scared us shitless. It wasn't until later we learned it was just latex and oil paint.

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: You kept freaking out on the way back home. It was so annoying.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Look who's talking. You were so freaked out, you couldn't say a single word. You ignored me the whole trip.

steps.name: Tall Woman and Roberta
steps.text: Hahahahaha!

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: Haha... *cough*...

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: (Quickly gives her a cup of water)

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Are you okay, Cynthia?

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: *gulp* *gulp*... I'm fine. So anyway, why did you ask me here today, Baker?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: A crew working on a historical drama came looking for me. They need a makeup artist to help them do up a whole gaggle of Victorian noblewomen. I'm thinking you might be the right girl for the job.

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: A Victorian period piece... We're talking elegant eyebrows and extravagant hairstyles? Interesting.

spans.text: A Victorian period piece... We're talking elegant eyebrows and extravagant hairstyles?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: It's funded by the Victorian government, so the budget's solid. The cast, director, and everyone's the best of the best in the industry. You'll make all kinds of connections.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: They'll see what you can do. And after this job, you won't ever have to worry about getting work again.

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: Nah... Maybe next time. I already told Mario I'd do his movie.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Please, Cynthia. Turn Mario down. This is the better opportunity.

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: Say what you want, disgusting, extreme, but those bloody scenes inspire me.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: You know you sound like a serial killer?

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: Good idea. Sounds like a fine career.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I'm not kidding. You need to think about your future.

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: I know the B-movies I work on have stupid plots full of holes and crude cinematography. I know they're so weird and out-there that audiences ignore them and the critics razz them.

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: But I don't care. I think there's nothing more awesome! My movies are brave enough to actually do stuff the mainstream films shy away from. The cookie-cutter blockbusters don't dare to imagine what the B-movies do.

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: They're eccentric, weird, absurd, and over-the-top. And that's what freedom means to me, it's what I've always dreamed of.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: But how are we supposed to chase our dreams with no food on the table?

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: Life is short, Baker. The more you want, the less you actually get. Sometimes, we have to focus on the things that we really want, instead of everything.

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: Tell me. Do you really like those pictures you work on? Is that 'refined taste' really worth pouring all your energy and effort into?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I... I don't know. It's all just work to me. I just do my job.

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: What about all the stuff that you've shelved? When will you go back to that?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: When I get the chance... I... I'll revisit them.

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: I can't wait, though!

steps.name: Tall Woman
steps.text: I'll never stop or compromise. I'm gonna do what I love every day, as long as I live, even if it only brings me pain.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Did you come up with something?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I just remembered a conversation we had. She said she was going to do what she liked.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: It was a cloudy day. The guy who owned the restaurant was so stingy that he didn't want to turn on a few more lights. It was completely dark, so I shouldn't have been able to see her face all that clearly...

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: But I still vividly remember her smile.
The face before her, white as a sheet of paper, overlaps with the face full of resolve and hope in Roberta's memories. She picks up her brush and starts painting the lifeless face.
As her brush applies the makeup foundation stroke after stroke, the face starts to become more vibrant, its dried out cheeks looking plump once more.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: (Sets down the brush)

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Are you finished?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Yeah, I'm done.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: It's like she's only sleeping. You know your stuff.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: You think so?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I've known her since I started in this industry.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Back then, I didn't have a penny to my name, and I couldn't find a place to stay. She took me into her little basement.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: After that, the two of us hopped from production to production, looking for work that could earn us a living.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: She was a first-class makeup artist. She could turn a face into something totally different.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: From the sound of it, she could've made a lot of money in Wrankwood.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: You need more than talent to make it big in Wrankwood. Her luck was rotten to begin with, but she was stubborn, too. She skipped every opportunity that came her way.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Seven years. We knew each other seven years. I remember how much energy she had when she got here, how she slaved away at night working on her projects, how excited she was when she got her first credit, and now...

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Now she's lying here in the morgue.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Ice cold, pale, and lifeless.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: But she looks much better after the makeup you did on her?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: No, this isn't what I wanted...

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Huh... Is it not good enough?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: What do you think...? If really did it right...

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Then why isn't she opening her eyes? Why isn't her heart beating? Why are her lips shut tight...?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Why is she just lying there... in silence?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Well... because she's dead.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Right... She's dead... Gone forever.
A sense of perplexity spreads from Roberta's face. At a loss, she simply looks at the tall, lifeless body.
With her guard down, the pain in her heart takes its chance to strike. The sharp sensation spreads out to every corner of her body.
At last, she finds herself unable to stand. She squats down into a ball, buries her face into her knees, and cries uncontrollably.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: If I was... just a little determined, just a little stubborn, would things have turned out different for her?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: What makes you say that?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: In Wrankwood, two things top the big studios' wishlists. First and foremost, they want people who follow orders. Next, they want technique. Your dreams and interests don't matter.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I know that better than anybody, but I gave up on pushing her. I couldn't do it.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Because... there was a voice in my heart that told me she was right.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: But I decided to ignore it. I couldn't keep going, like she did.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I made it all the way to today. I bowed my head to put food on the table.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I gave up and sacrificed a lot to stay commercial. And so my work became more and more successful.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: At the same time, my stuff got less interesting. I'm sure, one day, I'll be completely sick of it.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: But the excitement and joy she had never died down from the day she started in the business.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I think... with nothing else, that could've pushed her to make a name for herself.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I've always held out hope that her luck would turn around, that she'd be the exception to prove the rule. I really hoped for her... but I was wrong.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Sorry... I'm sorry, Cynthia.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Miss Baker. How... how is any of that your fault?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: (Cries uncontrollably)

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Sorry, I lost my cool.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Don't worry about it. People break down in here all the time. You actually kept it together pretty well.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: Honestly... The moment you sent her into the cremator, the thought of wiping all the makeup off crossed my mind.

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I was thinking, how could I let a peaceful sleeping face define her whole life?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I covered up all her life experience with makeup and forced a peaceful expression onto her... How is that any different from everything I gave up?

steps.name: Morgue Worker
steps.text: But you didn't... Why?

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: At the very moment... all of a sudden, I didn't wanna be a makeup artist anymore. I told myself, for just a second, I would become an embalmer who's committed to her work.

steps.name: Roberta
steps.text: I wanted to let her leave this world happy, even if it's all fake.
